categories.title: ElizaOS Token Community Sentiment and Project Activity Discussion

content.text: On July 28, 2026, community members in the ElizaOS Discord discussion channel expressed significant concern and frustration over the dramatic decline of the Eliza token, which had fallen from a peak market cap of approximately 2.4 billion dollars down to around 4 million dollars. Several users described the token as effectively dead with no clear path to recovery. One user noted that the only visible signs of ongoing development were GitHub commits, with lead developer Shaw reportedly active only on GitHub and not posting content directly related to ElizaOS on other platforms. Despite the bearish sentiment, at least one user disclosed they made a speculative purchase at the low price point, while another mentioned having inherited the token from the earlier ai16z era and having profited from a short trade. Questions were raised about whether the token is listed on any major exchanges beyond Kraken, and whether there were any meaningful announcements or signs of life from the team. One community member noted that an app appeared to be ready but questioned why there was no promotion of it on the main social media presence. The overall tone of the conversation reflected deep skepticism about the token's future value, with participants largely agreeing that only GitHub activity remained as evidence of any ongoing work.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Project Communication Concerns, Lawsuit Update, and Developer Announcements

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members expressed significant frustration over the lack of public communication from the ElizaOS team. User paolin raised concerns that while development activity is visible on GitHub and Shaw has posted occasionally on X about the Eliza app, all other official channels including Discord, X, and Farcaster have been largely inactive since late May. Paolin argued that the absence of regular updates is causing outsiders to assume the project is dead, and that this silence is damaging to community trust and potential investor interest. Paolin also noted that Shaw had previously pinned messages stating both Milady and Eliza v3 were nearing completion, but those milestones have not been publicly delivered, with no release date announced for the Eliza app. Paolin also suggested a token utility model where users would need to purchase and lock up ElizaOS tokens to access plugins and services, as a potential funding mechanism. User J_CHOY pushed back, arguing the team is actively building and shipping, pointing to GitHub activity and Shaw's posts on X as evidence. The exchange became heated, with both parties trading insults before other members called for more respectful dialogue. Separately, paolin shared a court document indicating that the lawsuit involving plaintiff Gorka Pikabea and the appearing defendants was dismissed with prejudice following a settlement, with the court retaining jurisdiction for 30 days to enforce the agreement, signed by Judge Jed S. Rakoff on July 8, 2026. User Omid Sa clarified that Eliza V3 was released some time ago and has been receiving updates, and can be accessed by cloning the main repository. Omid Sa also publicly requested that Shaw consider reinstating community member odlitime to the Discord. User Bek posted asking if anyone was looking for a developer.

In the coders channel, two external project announcements were made. User Kenhinde announced the launch of Coopa v4.0, described as a zero-trust digital data sovereignty platform built on top of Irys for permanent and immutable data storage. The platform uses wallet-based identity, requires no traditional cloud storage, and features a proprietary cryptographic layer. It is normally invite-only but was temporarily opened to the Irys community for stress testing, with feedback requested on upload speeds, wallet integration, and overall user experience. The platform is accessible at coopaassistant.com. Additionally, user x402 Data Hub announced the launch of x402 Data Hub, a real-time data API designed for autonomous AI agents. It provides access to LLM latency data, AI API pricing, cloud GPU rental indexes, and gas rates via HTTP 402 micro-payments at 0.01 USDC on Base and Arbitrum networks, with no API keys or signups required. Fifty free daily requests per dataset are available for developer testing.

categories.title: GOATNetwork Builder Grants Program and Community Activity

content.text: On July 30, 2026, community members exchanged greetings across the discussion and coders channels. A notable announcement was shared by Emmanuel promoting the GOATNetwork Builder Grants Program. The program is actively seeking teams building working products or MVPs, revenue-ready applications, AI agents solving real user problems, and agent-native apps that create repeatable onchain economic activity. Specific project types of interest include coding agents, research tools, workflow automation, sales and support agents, and agent-to-agent applications. Emmanuel offered to connect qualifying projects with the GOAT team via direct message. Separately, a community member named tomy.0315 posted in the discussion channel seeking freelance or long-term AI engineering opportunities, highlighting experience with AI agents, knowledge-base chatbots, voice assistants, and business automation systems. Another member asked how to open a support ticket.

In the discussion channel, a user inquired about something that was confirmed to be unofficial by D0CT0R. A suspicious recruitment message was posted by user Thehuuhs advertising job openings for the Shape3 ecosystem, claiming to seek Community Managers at 20-40 dollars per hour and Growth and Marketing Managers at 40-140 dollars per hour, with remote work and upfront payment. This same recruitment message was also cross-posted in the coders channel along with an attached image, suggesting coordinated spam activity across multiple channels.

In the coders channel, PnL Labs announced the release of a new plugin for Solana traders called plugin-pnllabs. The plugin is designed to allow agents to verify information before acting, including wallet trust based on realized on-chain profit and loss data, token safety checks, real trade cost analysis, and funding forensics. The team noted they audited 30 tracked smart money wallets and found that roughly half were actually losing money. The plugin is available via npm install at no cost for a free tier with no API key required, and uses a pay-per-call model through x402 after the free tier. The developer welcomed community feedback.

In the discussion channel, a user asked how to bridge funds from Base to Solana, though no answer was provided in the conversation. Separately, two users exchanged accusations of being scammers toward one another, with no resolution or moderation noted. Additionally, a user named Selcuk introduced a project called Coopa v4.0, which has been deployed on the Sepolia testnet. He described it as a zero-trust Digital Sanctuary that performs full client-side encryption before storing files and messages permanently on Irys and Arweave, meaning even the project servers cannot access stored data. Selcuk stated he is looking for power users to stress-test the architecture and provide honest feedback on the user experience. He shared the live app at coopaassistant.com and noted that Sepolia ETH for testing can be obtained at sepoliafaucet.com. He invited users to reply or send a direct message with bug reports or feature ideas.

In the coders channel, a few new members introduced themselves and asked questions about getting started. One user noted they were new to the community. Another user named Issa introduced themselves as a digital artist offering skills in animations and banners, asking if the team needed an artist or co-artist. A third user asked how to get started contributing to eliza.army and whether there were any starter documentation available, to which another community member confirmed that documentation exists. The channel topic directs users to the ElizaOS documentation site at docs.elizaos.ai to get started. The general discussion channel had no messages during this period.

categories.title: Community Discussion: Token Utility Concerns, Developer Outreach, and Project Activity

content.text: In the general discussion channel, a community member raised concerns about previously promised token-based utility that has not been delivered, questioning whether those statements were genuine or still planned. Another community member responded that users can add utility to the token and earn it. Separately, a developer posted asking if anyone was looking to hire a developer, which was met with hostility from another user who dismissed the request and made negative remarks about the project's development team. A different user then posted a detailed profile advertising their skills as a Senior AI and ML Full-Stack Engineer, highlighting experience with LLMs, agentic AI, RAG, automation, and various frameworks including LangGraph and OpenAI Agents SDK, with a background delivering AI products in Finance, Healthcare, and SaaS.

In the coders channel, a helper asked MochinoLabs whether the team had been in contact with them. MochinoLabs confirmed no contact had been made and asked where the getting started documentation was available online. The conversation moved to direct messages, though MochinoLabs later requested that communication return to the public channel or cease entirely.

In the partners channel, a community member with Partner and Vanguard roles noted signs of progress in the project repository, describing increased activity, models learning, harnesses merging, and suggesting that a significant development effort is underway.
